Name: Staphylococcus
Resistance: Strongest among nonspores; high salt tolerance; 90% penicillin-resistant.
Pathogenesis: Coagulase, SPA, staphylolysin, leukocidin, exfoliative toxin, TSST-1, enterotoxin.
Clinical: Local pyogenic infections (furuncle, carbuncle), bacteremia, SSSS, TSS, food poisoning.

Name: Streptococcus
Culture: Facultative anaerobe, requires enriched media; classified by hemolysis (α, β, γ).
Resistance: Weak; sensitive to normal antiseptics, penicillin, and erythromycin.
Pathogenesis: Hyaluronidase, SK, SD, Pyrogenic exotoxin, Streptolysin, M protein.
Clinical: Sore throat, pyoderma, erysipelas, scarlet fever, rheumatic fever.
Treatment: Penicillin (first choice); timely treatment of primary infection.

Name: E. coli
Morphology: Short rods, mostly possess peritrichous flagella & pili.
Culture: Lactose (+); forms pink, large colonies on SS medium.
Resistance: Susceptible to standard disinfectants; easily develops opportunistic drug resistance.
Pathogenesis: Pili, LT & ST enterotoxins, Shiga toxin.
Clinical: Extraintestinal (UTI, septicemia); Gastroenteritis via ETEC, EPEC, EHEC, EIEC, EAggEC.
Treatment: Stool/urine culture on SS agar; fluid management and antibiotics.

Name: Shigella
Morphology: Short rods; possess pili, no flagella.
Culture: Lactose (-); colorless, small colonies on SS medium.
Resistance: Weak, sensitive to acid; easily develops drug resistance.

Name: Salmonella
Morphology: Rods; possess pili and mostly peritrichous flagella.
Culture: Lactose (-); colorless colonies on SS medium.
Resistance: Easily killed by heat and chemical disinfectants.
Pathogenesis: Pili, endotoxin, enterotoxin; multiplies inside macrophages.
Clinical: Gastroenteritis, Enteric (Typhoid) fever, Septicemia; carrier state in gallbladder.
Treatment: Widal test; antibiotics; persistent cellular immunity post-recovery.

Name: Vibrio cholerae
Culture: Facultative anaerobic; requires alkaline environment (pH 8.5-9.5); cultured on TCBS.
Resistance: Weak; sensitive to acid/drying; dies at 100℃ in 2 minutes.
Treatment: Early diagnosis, quarantine, rapid rehydration, tetracycline/chloromycetin, vaccination.

Name: Clostridium tetani
Resistance: Very strong; spores survive boiling, killed only by autoclaving at 121℃ under pressure.
Clinical: Tetanus (lockjaw, spastic paralysis, severe muscle spasms).
Treatment: Debridement, TAT injection, penicillin, DPT vaccine (toxoids).

Name: Clostridium perfringens
Morphology: Large, rectangular bacilli; subterminal spore; capsule, non-motile.
Pathogenesis: α, β, ε, ι exotoxins (primarily α toxin) and enterotoxin.
Clinical: Gas gangrene; mild, self-limiting food poisoning.
Treatment: Debridement, hyperbaric oxygen, antitoxin, antimicrobial therapy.

Name: Clostridium botulinum
Morphology: Bacilli; subterminal oval spore ('tennis racket'); flagella present.
Resistance: Spores highly resistant; toxin is heat-labile.
Pathogenesis: Botulinum neurotoxin blocks release of acetylcholine.
Treatment: Heat food thoroughly, administer anti-toxin, antibiotic therapy if infected.
